title: Decision Lab marketplace
description: Decision tools organized into collections and use cases.

apps.name: Plan the first shipment
apps.description: Generate complete, static shipment plans from selectable lots, workers, preparation times, release time, carrier and departure. Check each whole plan against every declared readiness and travel scenario before comparing incremental expense. This synthetic operating snapshot does not infer readiness from business records or reserve stock, staff, authority or carrier capacity.

domain.label: Order fulfillment

useCase.label: Complete the first shipment
useCase.description: Compare complete shipment plans that must meet every mandatory obligation across the declared readiness and travel scenarios.

experience.question: Can we deliver the complete accepted order within its receipt, expense and cash limits?
experience.scope: A synthetic shipment with fixed lots, workers, preparation choices and carrier services. Times are synthetic days. Adapt the model for different operating catalogs.

apps.name: Compare release arrangements
apps.description: Compare four complete arrangements for an at-risk release. Reduced scope and a later date remain explicit amendments to the original commitment. This bounded calculation does not certify release quality or search all possible schedules.

domain.label: Software delivery
domain.description: Bounded operating decisions for software teams with explicit scope, capacity and timing.

useCase.label: Plan an at-risk release
useCase.description: Compare supplied arrangements while preserving the original release commitment.

experience.question: Which supplied release arrangements can satisfy the recorded scope, deadline, QA and spending requirements?
experience.scope: The authored build, environment, four release arrangements and transferable independent-regression package. Change recorded estimates, windows, fees and accepted amendments; adapt the author profile for a different release structure.

apps.name: Compare growth commitments
apps.description: Compare a current-approach baseline and three proposed growth commitments against cash by date, a required reserve, delivery capacity and a commitment cutoff. Forecast customer counts are uncertain situations, not controllable sales or probabilities. A feasible option is operationally supportable under these inputs; no most-profitable option is selected.

domain.label: Business growth
domain.description: Bounded growth commitments, operating capacity and the value of further learning.

useCase.label: Choose next month’s growth commitment
useCase.description: Find which supplied proposed growth commitments can be funded and delivered, then inspect what their spending must achieve.

experience.question: Which proposed growth commitments can we fund and deliver under the declared demand and collection situations?
experience.scope: A current-approach baseline and three proposed growth commitments for one standard service package. Change prices, committed campaign quotes, joint customer and collection forecasts, available cash, reserve and delivery-period capacity. A different service structure, installment contract or refund process needs an authored extension.

apps.name: Assess a payment-terms test
apps.description: Compare choosing a fundable and deliverable proposed growth commitment now with a nonbinding payment-preference test and a complete response to each possible signal.

experience.question: Could a timely preference test improve the growth choice enough to cover its cost?

apps.name: Compare learning-support plans
apps.description: Compare the next six-week support block for a fictional eight-year-old whose dyslexia and ADHD have already been professionally assessed. A positive classroom report can coexist with persistent decoding difficulty; renewing support on one overall success judgment could leave another need insufficiently addressed. Every response range is an authored assumption, not a validated prediction or a confidence interval. The classroom package is support for attention-related difficulties, not a complete clinical ADHD treatment. Separate progress measures inform reconsideration; before-and-after change alone does not establish a causal effect.

experience.question: Which support plan will help this child—and what improvement would show that it is working?
experience.scope: Compare the next six-week support block for a fictional eight-year-old whose dyslexia and ADHD have already been professionally assessed. A positive classroom report can coexist with persistent decoding difficulty; renewing support on one overall success judgment could leave another need insufficiently addressed. Every response range is an authored assumption, not a validated prediction or a confidence interval. The classroom package is support for attention-related difficulties, not a complete clinical ADHD treatment. Separate progress measures inform reconsideration; before-and-after change alone does not establish a causal effect.

apps.name: Understand reading, attention and language findings
apps.description: Review a bounded fictional record before turning poor grades into an either-or explanation. Separate what has been professionally recorded from what remains unassessed.

useCase.label: Understand reading, attention and language concerns

experience.question: What do the current assessment records establish about this child’s reading, attention and language difficulties, and what still needs assessment?
experience.scope: A fictional record-review example, not a diagnostic instrument. The finite catalogue describes possible professionally recorded reading, attention and language assessment conclusions, including coexistence and uncharacterized concerns. It is not an exhaustive catalogue of causes of poor grades. Only explicitly accepted, current records for the declared child, assessment episode and context constrain those possibilities. Logical agreement does not authenticate a record, establish clinical validity, attribute the cause of grades, prescribe support or estimate diagnostic probabilities.

apps.name: Review a release evaluation campaign
apps.description: Compare four authored GPU coordination policies for four sourced vLLM accuracy configurations. Timings are illustrative, unmeasured planning estimates. Inspect omitted work, slot use and deadlines.

experience.question: Which proposed arrangements plan every required evaluation within available GPU capacity and the review deadline?
experience.scope: Four sourced accuracy configurations and four authored policies. Change the deadline, slot count, timing estimates, compatibility assumption or bookings. Adapt the app for a different required workload. All starting timings are unmeasured estimates.

workflows.name: Plan a street-team deployment
workflows.description: Compare complete promotion plans against staffing, timing, recorded access and spending requirements, then calculate the additional guests needed to cover expense and separate discount loss. Choice and authorization remain outside the app; customer response is not forecast.

experience.question: Which promotion plans can we operate, and how many additional guests would cover their costs?
experience.scope: The authored street-team deployments with fixed deployment charges and same-day timing. Supply venue staffing, access, spending and contribution inputs; customer response is not forecast.

workflows.name: Repair a published restaurant roster
workflows.description: Compare complete repairs to a disrupted published restaurant roster across every remaining service. Check coverage, qualifications, availability, capacity, rest, hours and remaining payroll; optionally compare passing repairs by stability or payroll. The calculation compares supplied proposals and does not generate or publish a roster.

experience.question: Which supplied complete repairs cover every remaining service, and which fit the chosen priority?
experience.scope: The configured employees, service positions and four complete repair proposals. Change availability, payroll or comparison priority here; a different restaurant roster needs an adapted author profile.

workflows.name: Plan an at-risk release
workflows.description: Compare four complete release arrangements against remaining validation work, scoped qualifications, working intervals, resource commitments, additional spending, recorded prerequisites and permission. Keep the original scope and deadline distinct from explicitly accepted revisions. This bounded calculation does not predict delivery probabilities or replace a ticket system.

experience.question: This release is at risk. What can we still commit to?
experience.scope: A fictional release with four authored arrangements and fixed validation phases. Change the declared operating inputs; adapt the model for other scopes, work structures, resources or arrangements.

workflows.name: Choose next month’s growth commitment
workflows.description: Compare four complete growth commitments against cash after every dated payment and receipt, a required reserve, delivery hours, collection timing and the complete obligation horizon. Show the customer contribution needed to cover committed campaign spending. Optionally compare a nonbinding preference test using explicit probability assumptions and the same complete operating checks.

experience.question: Which growth plan can we afford to carry out?
experience.scope: A fictional service business with a current-approach baseline and three proposed growth commitments and one standardized package. Edit the explicit case values; adapt the app for other commitments, payment structures, activity dependencies or services.

workflows.name: Choose evidence before changing restaurant staffing
workflows.description: Compare choosing staffing now with a records audit or a complete four-dinner trial. Import all study-and-response operating constraints, charge each full evidence price once, and value noisy report responses over the stated future dinner horizon. Audit an optional actual report before reconsidering the remaining dinners from its original conditional probabilities.
